title: Remote foundations L1: host-to-central federation link over OpenSSH — A-initiated session per satellite with local and reverse forwards, a federation-only listener and pair-capability channel binding
outcome: Remote foundations L1: host-to-central federation link over OpenSSH — A-initiated session per satellite with local and reverse forwards, a federation-only listener and pair-capability channel binding
acceptance: The central host opens one OpenSSH session per enrolled satellite (batch mode, strict host-key checking, keepalive) that carries HTTP both ways: a local forward to the satellite and a reverse forward to the central host, each bound to loopback; it reuses the existing remote connector seams where possible. No UI or human relay is in the path.

Each forwarded listener mounts ONLY the federation routes, never the general local API; every request carries the pair capability and the receiving host binds the caller to exactly one enrolled peer by capability plus channel, never by a payload host id. Tests: a request without, or with another pair's, capability is refused; general API routes are unreachable through the forward.

Per-peer bounds: at most 4 in-flight RPCs, exponential backoff with jitter from 1 s to 5 min, no network I/O under the global state lock. Link incarnation is recorded so that stale replies after a reconnect are fenced (tests on one machine with two TermAl processes and a fake or loopback link).
Behind the M1 disabled-by-default setting; local behaviour unchanged.
Exact-input focused tests, the full five-stage gate and an independent review pair with no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
